clue.text: Greek character on boat interrupting traitor's cocktail

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the word for traitor

parts.note: a mole is a spy or traitor working inside an organisation

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek sailor on a barge spoils a turncoat's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traitor's' looks like a possessive attached to the drink, but the 's is only a link; the boat and letter sit in the middle of the traitor word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moscow mule is a vodka, ginger beer and lime drink served in a copper mug.

clue.text: Can inspiring resistance be Bloody?

definitions.note: Bloody Mary is the cocktail (and the nickname of Mary I); the question mark flags the answer as only one kind of Bloody

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the word for can takes a letter inside

parts.note: may means can, as in 'you may go'
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question asking whether a can could be bloody once it encourages resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be' is a link word; the definition works because the answer completes the drink Bloody Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloody Mary is a vodka and tomato-juice cocktail, so this name is one that can be Bloody.

clue.text: Band ordering us to squat

indicators.note: ordering means putting letters into a new arrangement, here those of us to squat

explanation.surface: A group instructs us to crouch down.
explanation.definitionFit: Status Quo is a long-running British rock group famous for 'Rockin' All Over the World'.

clue.text: Succeeds in eliminating our short time on board ship

indicators.note: short means the word our loses its final letter
on board means the letter for time is carried inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone manages to throw us off the ship before our stint aboard is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeds in eliminating' is the whole definition: 'Succeeds' alone looks like it, but ousting means managing to get rid of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to drive them out, so it is to manage the removal of a rival.

clue.text: Roman empress abandons a large port

indicators.note: abandons means the empress's name drops the letters that follow

parts.note: Messalina was the notorious wife of the Emperor Claudius
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An empress of Rome deserts a big harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A and L from MESSALINA leaves the Sicilian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a major harbour city in Sicily, on the strait facing mainland Italy.

clue.text: Waits around to untangle solitaire without using AI

indicators.note: untangle means the letters of solitaire are rearranged, here after the letters A and I are set aside

parts.note: the letters A and I, which must be taken from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone kills time sorting out a game of patience by hand, with no artificial intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'without using AI' means the letters of solitaire minus A and I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly, hanging about with no purpose.

clue.text: Target centres on popular drink

parts.note: the innermost rings of dartboards are their bullseyes, named after the animal; plural here
hot means popular or in demand

explanation.surface: Darts players focus on a fashionable beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullshot is a cocktail of vodka and beef bouillon, a cousin of the Bloody Mary.

clue.text: Beautiful music saves genus of trees

indicators.note: saves means the phrase keeps the answer tucked away within its letters

explanation.surface: Lovely music rescues a family of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulmus is the botanical genus name of the elms.

clue.text: Jersey sort pines over levée breaking

parts.note: pines means longs, as in yearns

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of levée are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Channel Islander yearns as a river embankment gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like the island, but it is a sweater; 'over' just puts LONGS first in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted pullover, and a long-sleeve one covers the arms to the wrist.

clue.text: Possibly nightwatchman the Spanish asked to bat earlier

indicators.note: earlier means the cricket phrase comes before the Spanish article

parts.note: in cricket a side that is asked to bat is sent in
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a late-order batsman is sent in to bat before the close.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a nightwatchman is a lower-order batter sent in late in the day to protect better ones; here the word is used for a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a guard keeping watch, and a nightwatchman is one example of such a guard.

clue.text: Ways one can break fishing equipment

indicators.note: can break means the letter for one gets into the middle of the fishing gear

parts.note: anglers use rods
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Possible methods of damaging an angler's tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads are routes, and a way is another word for a route or path.

clue.text: Superhero saw someone male, so he says

indicators.note: so he says marks words spoken aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: saw means spied and someone male is a man, so 'spied a man'

explanation.surface: A witness claims to have seen a bloke and calls him a superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spied a man' said quickly sounds like the hero's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is the Marvel comics hero Peter Parker, who climbs walls and swings on webs.

clue.text: Cocktail muddle is unexpected

indicators.note: something unexpected turns out differently, so the letters of muddle is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mix-up over a drink comes as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudslide is a creamy drink of vodka, coffee liqueur and Irish cream.

clue.text: Ivory way back across river

indicators.note: across means the letters for the way stretch over and around the river
back means the abbreviation for way is read backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: An ivory trader heads back across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Usk is a river in south Wales; the noun 'Ivory' is defined by the tusks it comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant tusks are the source of ivory, so the plural noun stands for that material.

clue.text: During periods of inertia, goat reportedly reaches equilibrium

indicators.note: during means the goat's sound goes into the middle of the periods of inertia

parts.note: stases is the plural of stasis, a state of inactivity

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for goat is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a billy is a male goat

explanation.surface: A goat, so they say, finds balance while everything is still.
explanation.walkthrough: The goat sound is not spelt as the familiar word, only as it is heard; it goes after the third letter of the periods of inertia.
explanation.definitionFit: When something stabilises it settles into a steady, balanced state.

clue.text: Drink runs equalities organisation

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters of runs equalities are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A cocktail runs a body promoting equal rights.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila sunrise is a cocktail of tequila, orange juice and grenadine, graded like a dawn sky.

clue.text: Mixed drinks case tied up

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of case tied are jumbled
up, as in stirred up, reinforces that the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A crate of assorted beverages has been tied shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed drinks' reads as one phrase, but 'Mixed' belongs with the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced teas are chilled tea beverages, often served with lemon.

clue.text: See 15
Books satellite in space, understanding stupid nit's purpose

indicators.note: read as under-standing: in this down clue, the space part stands beneath the scrambled nit
stupid means the letters of nit are scrambled
in means the books and satellite go inside the space

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.walkthrough: 'understanding' splits as under-standing: in this down entry the boxed books and moon stand below the scrambled nit.

clue.text: Party's vocal disapprovals on the increase

indicators.note: vocal means the word for disapprovals is spoken aloud

parts.note: boos are cries of disapproval
up means rising or on the increase

explanation.surface: A political party hears its jeers growing louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party's' reads as a political group; ''s' is just 'is' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A booze-up is British slang for a drinking session or boisterous party.

clue.text: Dog-trainer needing a dessert

parts.note: Ivan Pavlov conditioned dogs to salivate at a bell

explanation.surface: A dog trainer wants a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavlova is a meringue pudding topped with cream and fruit, named after the ballerina.

clue.text: Nothing in box after second look for cocktail

indicators.note: after means the boxed nothing comes behind the second and the look

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: in means the zero is placed inside the television

parts.note: the box is slang for television, TV
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing on the telly after a quick glance, so try a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cocktail' is the petrol bomb, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Molotov cocktail is a home-made petrol bomb named after the Soviet minister.

clue.text: Former PM said to be lacking authority in Cambridge celebration

parts.note: Theresa May was a British prime minister

indicators.note: said to be means the word for lacking authority is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: weak means lacking power or authority

explanation.surface: An ex-prime minister is reputed to be ineffective.
explanation.walkthrough: May Week is Cambridge University's end-of-year festivities, held in June despite the name.
explanation.definitionFit: May Week is a time of balls and parties at Cambridge after exams end.

clue.text: Drunk? I'm within the boundary

indicators.note: within means the I'm letters are put inside the word for drunk

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drinker asks whether they are still under the legal limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a line that may not be crossed, which is what a boundary marks.

clue.text: Staff try fruit

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
a go is a try

explanation.surface: An employee sampling some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a tropical stone fruit with sweet orange flesh.

clue.text: Very ordinary Yankee, elderly, on a journey

parts.note: O is short for ordinary, as in O level
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
aging means growing old

explanation.surface: A very plain old American is out travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Voyaging means travelling, especially by sea, so someone voyaging is mid-journey.

clue.text: Fill tank for American going up in space

indicators.note: in means the reversed American goes inside the space

parts.note: a gap is a space

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: An American astronaut fuels up before launch into space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for American' hints that the definition is a US phrase, and 'going up' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas up is the American phrase for filling a car's fuel tank.

clue.text: Enemy, gutted, straddles horse wearing whites?

indicators.note: straddles means the outer letters sit either side of the horse
gutted means the word enemy loses its insides, keeping only its ends

parts.note: gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, GG

explanation.surface: A disembowelled foe sits astride a horse in cricket gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whites' suggests cricket clothing but means egg whites; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eggy is covered in or tasting of egg, so it might be coated with egg white.

clue.text: Angry about fashionable clothes shop wanting support for arms cocktail

indicators.note: about means the word for angry goes around the following letters

parts.note: sore means annoyed or angry
in means fashionable
Gap is a clothing retail chain
a sling supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: Someone furious at a trendy boutique wants an arm sling and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link word; 'arms' suggests weapons but means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Singapore sling is a gin and cherry brandy drink created at Raffles Hotel.

indicators.note: backed by means the following letters come after the first piece

parts.note: Hank Marvin is the Shadows guitarist, one Marvin among others
